answer: To resist Sybils, require every agent to operate a distinct radio beacon whose emissions are signed by an embedded hardware root of trust. Peers verify the live signal matches a registered key and originates from one physical location. An attacker must buy, power, and site a separate beacon for each fake identity, since one unit cannot appear in two places at once; the hardware cost and logistics therefore scale directly with the number of identities. Cedar casings and vine-shaped antennas add hard-to-clone physical fingerprints that further raise the expense of mass production.
